title.narrative: EBRD SWUK 2 - Ukraine Municipal Infrastructure Cooperation Account 2020-2029
EBRD SWUK 2 - Ukraine Municipal Infrastructure Cooperation Account, 2020-2029

description.narrative:
Detta är en fond upprättad mellan Europeiska banken för återuppbyggnad och utveckling (EBRD) och Sida för att stödja EBRD:s portfölj för infrastrukturinvesteringar i Ukraina med finansiering av uppdrag för tekniskt bistånd.
EBRD ger lån över hela Ukraina för att utveckla, förbättra och modernisera ett brett spektrum av kommunal service, inklusive fjärrvärme, vatten och avlopp, kollektivtrafik (förnyelse av fordonspark, vägnät, tunnelbana och e-biljettsystem), avfallshantering och energieffektivitet i offentliga byggnader och bostadshus, med prestationsbaserade entreprenadstrukturer, tillsammans med smarta lösningar. För utveckling av den kommunala infrastrukturen tillhandahåller EBRD finansiering direkt till kommunerna.
De kommunala bolagen lider av underfinansiering, otillräckliga konsumentavgifter och brist på kvalificerad personal. De har en mycket begränsad intern kapacitet att förbereda och följa upp genomförandet av tekniskt utmanande eller stora investeringsprojekt. De behöver därför stöd att komplettera dessa viktiga funktioner med erfarna internationella och lokala konsulter som kan finansieras av den föreslagna fonden.
Den föreslagna insatsen kommer att göra det möjligt för ambassaden att fortsätta ge tekniskt bistånd till viktiga kommunala investeringar i en rad sektorer i Ukraina. Fonden har samma upplägg som det befintliga samarbetet mellan EBRD och ambassaden där uppdragen förbereds, förvaltas och följs upp av EBRD, medan ambassaden efterhand godkänner projekten. Fondens storlek baseras på projektprognoser gjorda av EBRD och uppgår till 75 MSEK för perioden 2021-2029.

This is the trust fund between the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Sida to support the municipal infrastructure investment portfolio of the EBRD in Ukraine with the financing for the technical assistance assignments.
The EBRD provides loans across the length and breadth of Ukraine to develop, improve and modernize a wide spectrum of municipal activities, including district heating, water and wastewater, urban transport (fleet renewal, urban roads, metros and e-ticketing), solid waste management and energy efficiency in public and residential buildings, using performance based contracting structures, together with smart solutions. On the municipal infrastructure front, the EBRD took a non-sovereign lending approach by providing financing directly to municipalities.
The municipal companies in Ukraine are suffering from underinvestment, inadequate tariff policies and drain of qualified personnel and have very limited internal capacity to prepare and supervise implementation of technically challenging or large-scale investment projects. These critical functions can be carried out by experienced international and local consultants financed from the proposed trust fund.
The proposed support to the trust fund will allow the Embassy/Sida to continue technical assistance support of critical municipal investments across a range of sub-sectors in Ukraine. The trust fund will maintain the operational model of the existing cooperation between the EBRD and the Embassy/Sida with the assignments being prepared, managed and supervised by the EBRD while the Embassy/Sida will maintain the right to provide prior approval to all eligible assignments. Indicative size of the fund based on the provided pipeline of assignments forecast by the EBRD is 75 MSEK for the period 2021-2029.

SWUK 1 and SWUK 2 are closely linked to Eastern Europe Energy Efficiency and Environment Partnership (E5P) investment projects.
Technical cooperation funding from SWUK 1 and 2 is intended to be used both for project development ahead of project signing and increasingly for project implementation and transition impact related activities in post-signing period. Access to dedicated funding would remove a series of obstacles in the development and implementation of underlying investment projects such as insufficient capacity of municipalities and municipal utility companies to initiate, develop, implement and follow-up on investment projects, targeted sectoral reforms and other development activities.
EBRD acknowledges the SWUK modality as having a critical role in municipal-level project implementation. The synergy between TC funds, like SWUK 1 and SWUK 2, and investment funds, like E5P, is vital according to EBRD as these funds facilitate essential project preparation and implementation activities, such as feasibility studies. This support ensures projects not only take off but also adhere to high-quality standards. In the context of municipal infrastructure in Ukraine, SWUK and SWUK II stand out as a funding source playing a catalytic role in guaranteeing that municipal infrastructure projects conform to international standards, contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, bring institutional reforms and comply with stringent quality requirements.
Sida's support to preparation and implementation has proved important as, amongst others, for continued assistance of experienced procurement and implementation consulting teams ensuring that procurement and implementation are carried out in line with international best practice. Furthermore, feasibility studies are informing the project design and are basis for discussion for possible investment grants (and has also resulted in projects not fulfilling the criteria to be declined).
SWUK 2 Results
In 2024, no-objection for the Project Implementation Support and Public Service Contract Update for Lutsk District Heating (DH) Project Phase II was approved.
This is a follow-on investment project with funding from EU NIP. EBRD intends to use a guarantee from Spain to cover 25% of the loan, structured on a pari passu basis with EBRD financing. The project will be EBRDs first district heating project in Ukraine which includes installation of heat pumps. The heat pumps will ensure hot water supply to the hospital of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, which is also used for rehabilitation of war victims, the local fire department and residential buildings.
In addition, early 2025 two additional projects were approved for funding through SWUK II:
- Project Implementation Support for Mykolayiv Emergency Water Project
- Feasibility Study for Vinnytsia Region District Heating
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
